disease_label_per_paper: Allograft adenovirus tubulointerstitial nephritis after kidney transplantation
presentation_summary: 63-year-old male presented six weeks after deceased donor renal transplant.
He had acute onset of fever, dysuria, hematuria, diarrhea, and acute graft dysfunction while on basiliximab induction and maintenance mycophenolate, tacrolimus, and prednisolone.
Urinalysis showed leukocytes, erythrocytes, and proteinuria; serum creatinine rose from a baseline of 150 umol/L to a peak of 300 umol/L.
Biopsy demonstrated necrotizing tubulointerstitial nephritis with viral cytopathic changes; adenovirus was identified by tissue PCR and urine PCR, and electron microscopy showed viral particles.
He improved after reduction of immunosuppression, IVIG, broad antimicrobial coverage, and ganciclovir given while CMV was being evaluated.

risk_context.source_text_value: delayed graft function with temporary dialysis

observations.source_text_value: basiliximab induction plus triple maintenance immunosuppression
acute graft dysfunction with creatinine doubling from baseline
allograft nephritis; local tenderness not numerically specified
observations.quality_note: Included as a moderate allograft inflammation signal because the paper emphasizes graft nephritis but does not quantify tenderness.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Allograft biopsy showed necrotizing tubulointerstitial nephritis of viral etiology
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: biopsy with viral cytopathic changes and tubular necrosis

confirmatory_findings.finding: Adenovirus identified in renal allograft by PCR
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: adenovirus identified in necrotic epithelial cells by PCR
urine viral PCR positive for adenovirus
electron microscopy showed 75 nm viral particles

actual_treatment: intravenous immunoglobulin total 32 g in five divided doses
ganciclovir while CMV PCR was pending
quality_warnings: Biopsy, PCR, and electron microscopy are confirmatory pathology/virology and are marked use_in_ranking:false.
Temperature, WBC, platelet, and exact urinalysis counts were not numerically available in the case text and were not invented.
Creatinine values were converted from umol/L to mg/dL using 88.4 umol/L per mg/dL.
